questions.stem: INDIA currently has how many STATES + UNION TERRITORIES?

options.option_text: 28 STATES + 8 UTs — post 2019 reorganisation of J&K (into UT J&K + UT Ladakh); Dadra+Nagar Haveli + Daman+Diu merged Jan 2020

questions.explanation: INDIA currently has 28 STATES + 8 UNION TERRITORIES (UTs) (2024). STATES (28 alphabetically — CAPITAL): (1) ANDHRA PRADESH — Amaravati (under construction) / currently de-facto Vijayawada-Visakhapatnam; Telugu. (2) ARUNACHAL PRADESH — ITANAGAR. (3) ASSAM — DISPUR (Guwahati); Assamese. (4) BIHAR — PATNA; Hindi. (5) CHHATTISGARH — RAIPUR (created 2000); Hindi. (6) GOA — PANAJI; Konkani. Smallest state. (7) GUJARAT — GANDHINAGAR. (8) HARYANA — CHANDIGARH (shared with Punjab — UT). (9) HIMACHAL PRADESH — SHIMLA; Hindi. (10) JHARKHAND — RANCHI (created 2000). (11) KARNATAKA — BENGALURU; Kannada. (12) KERALA — THIRUVANANTHAPURAM; Malayalam. (13) MADHYA PRADESH — BHOPAL. Largest state by area after Raj. (14) MAHARASHTRA — MUMBAI; Marathi. 2nd most populous. (15) MANIPUR — IMPHAL; Manipuri. (16) MEGHALAYA — SHILLONG; Khasi/English. (17) MIZORAM — AIZAWL; Mizo. (18) NAGALAND — KOHIMA; English. (19) ODISHA — BHUBANESWAR; Odia. (20) PUNJAB — CHANDIGARH (shared); Punjabi. (21) RAJASTHAN — JAIPUR. LARGEST state by area. (22) SIKKIM — GANGTOK; Nepali. Smallest population + 22nd state (1975 merger). (23) TAMIL NADU — CHENNAI; Tamil. (24) TELANGANA — HYDERABAD (shared with AP till 2014, full from 2024); Telugu. 29TH state created 2 JUN 2014. (25) TRIPURA — AGARTALA; Bengali. (26) UTTAR PRADESH — LUCKNOW; Hindi. MOST POPULOUS (~23 crore). If a country, would be 5th largest. (27) UTTARAKHAND — DEHRADUN (summer)/Gairsain (winter); Hindi. Formed 2000. (28) WEST BENGAL — KOLKATA; Bengali. UNION TERRITORIES (8): WITH LEGISLATURE: (a) DELHI (National Capital Territory; CM Arvind Kejriwal AAP 2013-, now 3rd term; 70 seats). (b) PUDUCHERRY (former French colonies, Puducherry + Mahé + Karaikal + Yanam; CM N Rangasamy AINRC 2021-; 30 seats). (c) J&K (since 31 Oct 2019; first elections Sep-Oct 2024; CM Omar Abdullah NC+Cong 2024-). WITHOUT LEGISLATURE (directly under President via LG/Administrator): (d) CHANDIGARH — shared capital Punjab+Haryana. (e) ANDAMAN + NICOBAR ISLANDS — Port Blair (renamed Shri Vijaya Puram in 2024). (f) LAKSHADWEEP — Kavaratti. (g) DADRA + NAGAR HAVELI + DAMAN + DIU (merged 26 Jan 2020; HQ Daman). (h) LADAKH (since 31 Oct 2019; Leh + Kargil; demands full statehood + 6th Schedule tribal protection). TOTAL = 36 (28+8). RECENT reorganisation: (a) 2014 (2 Jun) — TELANGANA formed from AP (29th state). (b) 2019 (31 Oct) — J&K state BIFURCATED into 2 UTs (J&K with LA + Ladakh without LA); Art 370 abrogated. (c) 2020 (26 Jan) — Dadra + NH + Daman + Diu UTs merged (had been separate). State count 28 + UT count 8. STATE ORDER OF CREATION: Andhra State (1953, first linguistic); Gujarat + Maharashtra (1960, from Bombay); Nagaland 1963; Haryana 1966; HP full state 1971; Meghalaya, Manipur, Tripura 1972; Sikkim 1975; Mizoram + Arunachal + Goa 1987; Chhattisgarh + Uttarakhand + Jharkhand 2000; Telangana 2014. PENDING state demands: Gorkhaland (WB), Vidarbha (Maharashtra), Bundelkhand, Bodoland, Harit Pradesh (UP), Kodagu, Greater Tipraland, Saurashtra, Mithilanchal, Kongu Nadu, Panruti. ART 3 of Constitution empowers PARLIAMENT to form/alter states.

questions.stem: The LARGEST Indian state by AREA is:

options.option_text: RAJASTHAN — 3,42,239 sq km (~10.4% of India's area); desert-heavy (Thar); capital Jaipur; largest by area since formation 1956

questions.explanation: INDIAN STATES by AREA (top 10, 2024): (1) RAJASTHAN — 342,239 sq km (10.4%). Capital JAIPUR. Known for: Thar Desert (Sahara of India), Mughal-Rajput architecture, princely palaces, Pushkar camel fair, Kaziranga... er Ranthambore tigers. Bordered by Pakistan + 5 states. (2) MADHYA PRADESH — 308,252 sq km. Capital BHOPAL. 'Heart of India' — central India. Tiger reserves (Kanha, Bandhavgarh, Pench, Panna). Ujjain, Khajuraho (UNESCO), Gwalior, Indore (cleanest city 6 years). Highest tribal population state. (3) MAHARASHTRA — 307,713 sq km. Capital MUMBAI (financial capital of India; 'maximum city'); RTE + Bollywood + Ajanta-Ellora UNESCO + Shivaji's Raigad + Ganapati Pune + Nasik Kumbh. 2nd most populous state. (4) UTTAR PRADESH — 240,928 sq km. Capital LUCKNOW. MOST POPULOUS state (~23 crore). Taj Mahal + Varanasi + Ayodhya + Prayagraj Kumbh + Mathura + Agra. Has ~28% of nation's population on ~7% land. Divides into 75 districts; Hindi heartland. (5) GUJARAT — 196,024 sq km. Capital GANDHINAGAR. 'India's Jewel' business state. Modi home state. Statue of Unity (182m, world's tallest). Rann of Kutch + Gir lions. Surat diamond city. (6) KARNATAKA — 191,791 sq km. Capital BENGALURU (IT capital of India). Hampi, Coorg, Mysore. Kannada heritage + Bhakti saints. (7) ANDHRA PRADESH — 162,968 sq km (post-Telangana). Capital Amaravati (planned). Telugu heritage; Tirupati temple; Araku Valley. (8) ODISHA — 155,707 sq km. Capital BHUBANESWAR. Puri Jagannath, Konark, Chilika lake, Sun Temple, tribal culture + Kalinga legacy. (9) CHHATTISGARH — 135,192 sq km. Capital RAIPUR. Carved from MP 2000. Tribal heartland; Bastar, Jagdalpur. (10) TAMIL NADU — 130,058 sq km. Capital CHENNAI. Dravidian culture + Carnatic music + classical Tamil. STATES by POPULATION (top 10, 2011 census projected to 2024): (1) UP ~23 cr; (2) Maharashtra ~13 cr; (3) Bihar ~13 cr; (4) West Bengal ~10 cr; (5) MP ~8.6 cr; (6) TN ~8 cr; (7) Rajasthan ~8 cr; (8) Karnataka ~6.9 cr; (9) Gujarat ~6.8 cr; (10) Andhra ~5.2 cr. SMALLEST states: (a) by AREA — GOA (3,702 sq km; smallest state), SIKKIM (7,096 sq km); (b) by POPULATION — SIKKIM (~7 lakh; smallest), Mizoram, Arunachal. UTs by area: (a) Largest UT = LADAKH (59,146 sq km — larger than Kerala + Punjab); (b) Smallest UT = LAKSHADWEEP (32 sq km). MOST DENSELY POPULATED: Delhi UT (11,297/sq km), Bihar (1,106), WB (1,028), Kerala (859). LEAST DENSELY POPULATED: Arunachal (17/sq km), Mizoram (52), Sikkim (86), Manipur (128). INDIA's TOTAL AREA: 3,287,263 sq km = 7th largest country. INDIA's POPULATION: ~144 crore (2024, world's most populous since April 2023).

questions.stem: The capital of ANDHRA PRADESH (post-Telangana split 2014) is:

options.option_text: AMARAVATI (planned greenfield capital on Krishna riverbank) — but political flux; Chandrababu Naidu revived Jan 2025 after YSRCP's 3-capital plan scrapped

questions.explanation: ANDHRA PRADESH CAPITAL SAGA — complex post-Telangana bifurcation (2 JUNE 2014). BACKGROUND: (1) Under ANDHRA PRADESH REORGANISATION ACT 2014, HYDERABAD was to be JOINT CAPITAL of AP + Telangana for 10 YEARS (till 2 JUN 2024; this deadline passed; now Hyderabad is solely Telangana's). (2) Residual AP had to build NEW CAPITAL. CM N. Chandrababu Naidu (TDP, 2014-19) chose AMARAVATI — greenfield city on south bank of Krishna river; adjacent to historic Amaravati (Buddhist heritage; capital of Satavahanas 2,000 yrs ago). Architects: Norman Foster + others (visionary design). Hindi World Capital funds + Singapore consultancy. Inaugurated capital city construction 2014-19. ~33,000 acres land pooled from farmers. Progress was made but... (3) 2019 — Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy (YSRCP) became CM; HALTED Amaravati + proposed '3 CAPITALS' — (a) AMARAVATI = LEGISLATIVE capital; (b) VISAKHAPATNAM = EXECUTIVE capital; (c) KURNOOL = JUDICIAL capital. Modelled on South Africa. Passed AP Decentralisation Acts 2020. Massive protests from Amaravati farmers (who had pooled land). HC struck down Acts 2022. Govt appealed to SC. STALEMATE throughout 2019-24. (4) 2024 (May-June) — TDP-Jana Sena-BJP alliance WON AP elections; N Chandrababu Naidu RETURNED as CM. Revived AMARAVATI as sole capital; Jan 2025 formally restored Amaravati Capital City masterplan. PROGRESS: Secretariat + Assembly + HC buildings under-construction (paused 2019-24); farmer trust to be restored. Target 2027-29 for usable capital. TEMP AP ARRANGEMENT: as of 2024-25, government operates partly from Vijayawada + Guntur (core Amaravati area); HC at Amaravati; some at Visakhapatnam. TRULY unique — probably world's MOST INTERRUPTED capital project. OTHER STATE CAPITAL MOVES in INDIAN HISTORY: (1) DELHI — shifted from Calcutta in 1911 (Delhi Durbar); inaugurated 1931. (2) CHHATTISGARH — new capital RAIPUR from formation 2000. (3) JHARKHAND — Ranchi from 2000. (4) UTTARAKHAND — DEHRADUN temporary since 2000; planned GAIRSAIN (Chamoli, Himalayan foothills) as summer capital since 2020. (5) HIMACHAL PRADESH — SHIMLA (from early 1864 British hill station — still India's busiest tourist hill station; now overcrowded). (6) RECENT demands: KARNATAKA ('Greater Bengaluru'), UP (Noida as hub)... NEW CAPITAL examples globally: (a) BRASILIA (Brazil, 1960) — Lucio Costa + Niemeyer. (b) CANBERRA (Australia, 1927). (c) ISLAMABAD (Pakistan, 1967). (d) DODOMA (Tanzania, 1974). (e) ABUJA (Nigeria, 1991). (f) ASTANA/NUR-SULTAN (Kazakhstan, 1997; restored to Astana 2022). (g) NAYPYIDAW (Myanmar, 2005, secretive). (h) NUSANTARA (Indonesia, 2024 — East Kalimantan, moving from Jakarta due to sinking + congestion). AMARAVATI is one of world's most ambitious + politically fraught greenfield capitals. India's earlier Naya Raipur, Gandhinagar, Chandigarh, Bhubaneswar are greenfield capitals.

options.option_text: THIRUVANANTHAPURAM (formerly TRIVANDRUM) — southern-most state capital; 'abode of Ananta (Vishnu)' Hindu mythology; seat of Kerala Legislative Assembly

questions.explanation: KERALA ('God's Own Country' — tourism tagline) — one of India's most culturally + environmentally distinctive states. Capital: THIRUVANANTHAPURAM (formerly TRIVANDRUM). Name means 'abode of Ananta' (the serpent on which Vishnu reclines — from SRI PADMANABHASWAMY TEMPLE's deity). Southernmost state capital. KERALA FACTS: (1) FORMATION: 1 November 1956 (Kerala Piravi Day) — linguistic reorganisation combining Malabar (Madras) + Travancore + Cochin. (2) MALAYALAM — official language; palindrome name. (3) 38,863 sq km area; 3.5 crore population. (4) HIGHEST LITERACY RATE in India — 94% (NFHS-5); declared FULLY LITERATE 1991 by NLM; 2024 survey found effective 96%+. (5) Sex ratio 1,084 females/1000 males — BEST in India. (6) Highest LIFE EXPECTANCY — 75 years (national 70). (7) Lowest IMR (Infant Mortality Rate) — 4 per 1000 live births (national 27). (8) HDI rank 1 among Indian states. (9) KERALA MODEL of DEVELOPMENT — high human-development indicators despite middle per-capita income; achieved via land reforms + education + health investments + leftist + matrilineal Nair/Nampudri social traditions + remittances from Gulf. (10) REMITTANCES — ~20% of GSDP; 23+ lakh Keralite expatriates abroad (mostly Gulf). (11) ECONOMY — tourism + remittances + services dominant; agri (coconuts, spices, tea, rubber) + fisheries. (12) BACKWATERS — famous CANOE-DOTTED network of lagoons + lakes + rivers; Alappuzha/Alleppey + Kumarakom + Kottayam + Kollam; HOUSE BOATS popular tourist draw. (13) WESTERN GHATS — UNESCO WHS (2012). (14) 4 UNESCO WHS sites in Kerala's broader region. (15) HIGH OUTMIGRATION — best-educated youth leaving for jobs. (16) RESPECTFUL COMMUNISM — only Indian state where CPI(M) has sustained electoral base; LDF-UDF alternate rule; current LDF govt (Pinarayi Vijayan CM since 2016, 2021-26). MAJOR TOURIST DESTINATIONS: (a) THIRUVANANTHAPURAM — Padmanabhaswamy Temple (richest temple in world — vaults opened 2011 revealed $22 billion treasure). Napier Museum, Shanghumukham Beach, Kovalam beach. (b) KOCHI — commercial capital, port city. Mattancherry Palace + Jewish synagogue (Paradesi, 1568). Fort Kochi. Chinese fishing nets. Kochi-Muziris Biennale. (c) ALAPPUZHA (Alleppey) — 'Venice of the East'; backwaters + Nehru Trophy Boat Race. (d) MUNNAR — tea plantations in hills. (e) WAYANAD — wildlife + edakkal caves. (f) THEKKADY (Periyar) — wildlife sanctuary. (g) KUMARAKOM — backwaters + birds. (h) KOVALAM — beaches. (i) VARKALA — cliff beach. (j) BEKAL — Arabian Sea fort. (k) PARAMBIKULAM + SILENT VALLEY — biosphere reserves. (l) SABARIMALA — Ayyappa temple (pilgrimage site; 2018 SC-allowed women's entry ruling sparked protests). (m) CHERAI Beach. CUISINE: KERALA + BANANA CHIPS + PARATHA (CF PAROTTA/MALABAR) + CHICKEN STEW + APPAM + KADALA + meen moilee (fish) + sadhya (22-dish feast on banana leaf) + coconut every dish. OKU (onam) + VISHU + Christmas major festivals. ONAM — 10-day festival end-Aug/Sep celebrating King Mahabali's annual return. KATHAKALI + MOHINIYATTAM + KUDIYATTAM + KALARIPAYATTU martial art. MALAYALAM CINEMA — Adoor Gopalakrishnan, Shaji Karun, Aravindan, recent MANI RATNAM, Lijo Jose Pellissery, parallel cinema tradition. MAJOR AIRPORTS: Trivandrum + Kochi + Calicut + Kannur. Major PORTS: Cochin (oldest + transhipment hub) + Vizhinjam (Adani's new deepwater port, 2024). India's first indigenously-built Rocket-Launch Pad = TERLS Thumba Thiruvananthapuram.

questions.stem: India's 7 SISTER STATES of the NORTH EAST + 1 'brother' state are:

options.option_text: Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, WB, Sikkim, Assam, Manipur, Tripura
'7 SISTERS' — ARUNACHAL PRADESH, ASSAM, MANIPUR, MEGHALAYA, MIZORAM, NAGALAND, TRIPURA + SIKKIM as 'brother' (8th NE state)

questions.explanation: NORTH-EAST INDIA / NORTH EASTERN STATES — 8 states: the '7 SISTERS' + SIKKIM ('one brother'). (1) ASSAM (1 Apr 1912 as Assam Province; full state 1947); Capital DISPUR (Guwahati suburb). Largest NE state. Language: Assamese. GDP largest in NE. MANY indigenous groups; Tea + oil + tourism. Kaziranga (one-horned rhino UNESCO), Majuli (world's largest river island). (2) ARUNACHAL PRADESH (UT 1972 → State 20 Feb 1987). Capital ITANAGAR. 'LAND OF DAWN-LIT MOUNTAINS'. Largest NE state by area. 26 major tribes + 100 sub-tribes — most tribal diversity. Tawang monastery (biggest in India, 2nd in world; Dalai Lama's 1959 escape refuge). India-China border (disputed — Arunachal is claimed by China as 'South Tibet'). Close to Brahmaputra source. (3) MANIPUR ('jewel of India') — UT 1972 → State 21 Jan 1972. Capital IMPHAL. Language: Meiteilon (Manipuri). Sangai deer unique. LOKTAK LAKE + KEIBUL LAMJAO (world's only FLOATING national park). Famous WOMEN-only market (Ima Keithel, Imphal). Polo + Ras Leela + Thang-Ta martial art. INA HQ was here (Netaji's Provisional Govt). 2023 Meitei-Kuki communal violence (ongoing crisis). (4) MEGHALAYA ('abode of clouds') — carved from Assam 21 Jan 1972. Capital SHILLONG (Scotland of East). Language: Khasi (but English also official). WETTEST places in world — CHERRAPUNJI + MAWSYNRAM. Living root bridges (Khasi tribal engineering). DAWKI-Umngot river. Matrilineal (Khasi, Jaintia, Garo tribes — inheritance via youngest daughter). (5) MIZORAM (lit 'land of Mizo people') — UT 1972 → State 20 Feb 1987. Capital AIZAWL. Language: Mizo. ~87% Christian (highest among states); ~91% literate. Bamboo architecture + dances. HORTICULTURE hub. (6) NAGALAND — 1 Dec 1963 (16th state). Capital KOHIMA. Language: English (official; Nagamese is lingua franca). 16+ tribes — each with distinct culture + language. HORNBILL FESTIVAL (1-10 Dec, Kisama Heritage Village near Kohima) — showcase of all tribes. Battle of Kohima (1944) = turning point in WWII Burma campaign. (7) TRIPURA — UT 1972 → State 21 Jan 1972. Capital AGARTALA. Language: Bengali + Kokborok (tribal). Manikya dynasty ruled for 600+ years. (8) SIKKIM — 22ND STATE of INDIA (merged 16 MAY 1975 via referendum; earlier protectorate). Capital GANGTOK. Languages: Nepali, Bhutia, Lepcha (+ more). Kanchenjunga (Khangchendzonga) — India's tallest peak + world's 3rd tallest (8,586m; UNESCO Mixed Heritage since 2016); sacred to Sikkimese. FIRST fully ORGANIC farming state (2016). Bhutia + Lepcha + Nepali ethnic groups. NORTH EAST GOVERNANCE: 6TH SCHEDULE areas in (a) Meghalaya (Khasi, Jaintia, Garo Autonomous Councils); (b) Mizoram (Chakma, Mara, Lai Autonomous District Councils); (c) Tripura (TTAADC). 5TH SCHEDULE areas also. INSURGENCIES historically (now largely resolved): ULFA (Assam), NSCN (Nagaland — Naga Peace Accord 2015), HNLC (Meghalaya), DHD (Dima Hasao Assam), BLT/NDFB (Bodo Assam — 2020 Bodo Peace Accord). AFSPA (Armed Forces Special Powers Act 1958) still in force in parts. Infrastructure push: 100+ airports opened; BOGIBEEL BRIDGE (Assam 2018, India's longest rail-road bridge 4.94 km); Act East Policy (since 2014).

questions.stem: KANCHENJUNGA, India's TALLEST PEAK (8,586 m — world's 3rd tallest), is located on the border of:

options.option_text: SIKKIM (India) + NEPAL — highest peak in India; UNESCO Mixed Heritage Site (Khangchendzonga NP); sacred to Sikkimese; K₂ (higher) is in POK disputed area

questions.explanation: KANCHENJUNGA (Khangchendzonga, 'Five Treasures of Snow') — 8,586 METRES (28,169 ft) — WORLD's 3rd HIGHEST MOUNTAIN + HIGHEST PEAK IN INDIA. Straddles SIKKIM-NEPAL border. First climbed 25 May 1955 by a British expedition (Joe Brown + George Band stopped just below the summit out of respect for the local Sikkimese belief that the summit is sacred — tradition continues; climbers still leave last few metres unclimbed). Name from Tibetan — 5 treasures of snow (gold, silver, gems, grain, holy books). KHANGCHENDZONGA NP — UNESCO MIXED Heritage site (2016, first in India for Mixed — natural + cultural); covers Kanchenjunga + 18 glaciers + diverse biodiversity + tribal sacred sites. 8000+ METRE PEAKS of the world (14 total, all in Himalayas + Karakoram, 'EIGHT-THOUSANDERS'): (1) MT EVEREST (8,848 m; Nepal-China; highest). (2) K2 (8,611 m; Pakistan-China; GILGIT-Baltistan area claimed by India as part of PoK). (3) KANCHENJUNGA (8,586 m). (4) Lhotse (8,516 m Nepal). (5) Makalu (8,481 m Nepal-China). (6) Cho Oyu (8,188 m Nepal-China). (7) Dhaulagiri (8,167 m Nepal). (8) Manaslu (8,163 m Nepal). (9) Nanga Parbat (8,126 m Pakistan). (10) Annapurna I (8,091 m Nepal). (11) Gasherbrum I (8,080 m; PoK). (12) Broad Peak (8,051 m; PoK). (13) Gasherbrum II (8,035 m; PoK). (14) Shishapangma (8,027 m; Tibet/China only — sole all-in-one-country 8000er; opened to climbers late). MOUNTAINS of INDIA (highest peaks by state, undisputed only — so excluding K2 + Gilgit peaks): (1) KANCHENJUNGA 8586 (Sikkim, India's tallest). (2) NANDA DEVI 7816 m (Uttarakhand; India's 2nd tallest; 2nd highest in India proper). (3) KAMET 7756 m (Uttarakhand). (4) SALTORO KANGRI 7742 m (Ladakh). (5) Mana Peak 7272 m (UK). (6) Mamostong Kangri 7516 (Ladakh). MINOR PEAKS: Munsiyari (UK), Roopkund (UK, mysterious skeletons lake), Chandra Taal (HP). MOUNTAINEERS from INDIA: (1) TENZING NORGAY — Sherpa (of Darjeeling Indian origin ambiguity, later Indian citizen); co-summit of Everest 29 May 1953 with Sir Edmund Hillary (NZ). Tenzing was IMF President 1954; Padma Bhushan 1959. (2) BACHENDRI PAL — FIRST INDIAN WOMAN on EVEREST (23 May 1984); 1st Indian + 5th woman in world. Padma Shri 1984, Padma Bhushan 2019. (3) SANTOSH YADAV — 1st woman TWICE on Everest (1992 + 1993). (4) ARUNIMA SINHA — 1st AMPUTEE WOMAN on Everest (2013; lost leg in train push by robbers 2011). (5) 13-year-old POORNA MALAVATH (Telangana, 2014) — youngest girl to summit Everest. (6) MALAVATH POORNA + SUSHMA SINGH + SATYARUP SIDDHANTA + various Army + IAF expeditions. INDIAN MOUNTAINEERING FOUNDATION (IMF, 1958, Delhi) regulates climbing. NEHRU INSTITUTE OF MOUNTAINEERING (NIM, Uttarkashi), HMI (Himalayan Mountaineering Institute, Darjeeling 1954 — Tenzing was founding director), ABVIMAS (Manali), JIM (Pahalgam), NIMAS (Sikkim) — key training institutes.

questions.stem: The FIRST STATE in INDIA to be created on PURELY LINGUISTIC basis was:

options.option_text: ANDHRA STATE (1 October 1953) — carved from Madras State after POTTI SRIRAMULU's 56-day fast-unto-death for Telugu state; catalyst for States Reorganisation 1956

questions.explanation: ANDHRA STATE — formed on 1 OCTOBER 1953 as FIRST LINGUISTIC state of independent India (Telugu-speaking majority carved from Madras State). Later merged with Telangana region of HYDERABAD state on 1 Nov 1956 (linguistic reorganisation) to form modern ANDHRA PRADESH. Further bifurcated 2014 into Andhra Pradesh + Telangana. POTTI SRIRAMULU (1901-1952) — Telugu linguistic leader; Gandhian + social reformer. His 56-DAY FAST-UNTO-DEATH at Madras demanding separate Andhra State led to his death on 15 DEC 1952 in a state of political indifference from Nehru + Congress. MASS UPHEAVAL in Andhra region after his death; riots; 7 killed in police firing. JAWAHARLAL NEHRU conceded — announced new Andhra state formation in Dec 1952; effective 1 OCT 1953. Sriramulu = 'AMARAJEEVI' ('immortal being'). This event CATALYSED the CONVENING of STATES REORGANISATION COMMISSION (SRC) in 1953 — Fazl Ali + K.M. Panikkar + H.N. Kunzru. Submitted report Oct 1955. STATES REORGANISATION ACT 1956 (1 Nov 1956) — India reorganised into 14 STATES + 6 UTs on PRIMARILY LINGUISTIC basis. LANGUAGES in India's 8TH SCHEDULE: (1) originally 14 at Constitution adoption 1950 — Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Kashmiri, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu. (2) Sindhi added 1967 (21st CAA). (3) Konkani + Manipuri + Nepali added 1992 (71st CAA). (4) Bodo + Dogri + Maithili + Santhali added 2003 (92nd CAA). Current: 22 SCHEDULED LANGUAGES. PENDING: RAJASTHANI, BHOJPURI, MAGAHI, TULU, KHASI, MIZO, GARO, KODAVA, KHORTHA, KUMAONI, GARHWALI, BHOJPURI, ENGLISH etc. demanded. CLASSICAL LANGUAGES (6 + new additions Oct 2024) — ministry of culture recognition with criteria (1500-2000 years old + independent traditions + ancient literature + not subsidiary): (1) TAMIL (2004 — first); (2) SANSKRIT (2005); (3) TELUGU (2008); (4) KANNADA (2008); (5) MALAYALAM (2013); (6) ODIA (2014). Added Oct 2024 (Modi cabinet): (7) MARATHI; (8) PALI; (9) PRAKRIT; (10) ASSAMESE; (11) BENGALI. HINDI not in classical (younger). OFFICIAL LANGUAGES: (a) UNION — HINDI (Devanagari) + ENGLISH (as per Official Languages Act 1963 for associate purpose, continuation via amendments). (b) STATE — various under Art 345 + 347; each state can notify its own. (c) Scheduled languages have protections under Art 344 (Official Language Commission) + Art 348 (SC + HC use) + Art 351 (Hindi development). LINGUISTIC ORGANISATION has been SUCCESSFUL + stabilising for India. States' cultural + political identity strengthened. Bilingual Bombay (split 1960 Gujarat + Maharashtra); Trilingual Punjab (split 1966 Punjab + Haryana + HP additions); Khasi+Jaintia+Garo tribal Meghalaya, Manipuri etc. Further linguistic/ethnic demands continue: BODOLAND (Assam Bodo), GORKHALAND (WB Nepali), KAMTAPUR (WB Koch-Rajbongshi), MITHILANCHAL (Maithili Bihar), TULUNADU (Tulu Karnataka), KONGU NADU (TN), VIDARBHA (Marathi Maha), KODAVA (Karnataka).

questions.stem: The NEWEST (29th) state of INDIA is:

options.option_text: TELANGANA — formed 2 June 2014 (bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh); Hyderabad as shared capital till June 2024, now solely Telangana's; first CM K. Chandrashekar Rao

questions.explanation: TELANGANA — 29TH STATE of INDIA; formed 2 JUNE 2014. Bifurcation of ANDHRA PRADESH via ANDHRA PRADESH REORGANISATION ACT 2014. Capital: HYDERABAD (shared with residual AP till 2 June 2024 per 10-year transition clause; now SOLELY Telangana's). Area: 112,077 sq km (12th largest). Population ~3.5 crore. Language: TELUGU. LONG demand — ~60 YEARS of struggle + mobilisation. BACKGROUND: (1) Telangana region = former HYDERABAD state (Nizam's dominion, integrated 1948). (2) Merged with Andhra (ex-Madras) to form ANDHRA PRADESH on 1 NOV 1956 per Gentleman's Agreement with safeguards for Telangana. (3) Safeguards not fully implemented; perception of discrimination by coastal Andhra + Rayalaseema elites in jobs, water, education, resources. (4) 1969 first Telangana agitation (Marri Chenna Reddy); Separate Telangana Praja Samithi. (5) 2001 — K. CHANDRASHEKAR RAO (KCR) split from TDP to form TELANGANA RASHTRA SAMITHI (TRS) with single-point agenda. (6) KCR's 11-day fast 2009 (Nov-Dec 2009) forced Centre (Chidambaram) to announce Telangana would be carved out. Rollback due to coastal Andhra agitation; years of turmoil. (7) Oct 2011 — 'Million March' Hyderabad. (8) 2014 — UPA-II govt pushed Bifurcation Bill through Parliament despite chaos (pepper spray incidents in LS); passed 18 Feb 2014. Presidential assent 1 March 2014. (9) 2 JUN 2014 — Telangana became 29th state; KCR sworn in as 1st CM; TRS won 2014 + 2018 elections. (10) 2023 Dec elections: CONGRESS won; A. REVANTH REDDY became CM (7 Dec 2023). KCR OUT. TRS renamed BHARAT RASHTRA SAMITHI (BRS) 2022 to go national. KEY FACTS: (1) Telangana has 33 districts (up from 10 initial). (2) First state in INDIA to offer ₹3L crore DBT farm welfare (RYTHU BANDHU since 2018 — ₹10,000/acre/year to farmers). (3) PADDY + cotton + turmeric + chilli top crops. (4) Hyderabad = 'CYBERABAD' + 'GENOME VALLEY' — IT + Pharma + biotech hub; Microsoft largest campus outside Redmond. (5) KALESHWARAM PROJECT — world's largest multi-stage lift irrigation (Godavari); cost ₹1 lakh crore; controversy. (6) TS-Kisan Call Centre, Mission Bhagiratha (drinking water), 2BHK free houses schemes. (7) Literacy ~66%. (8) Kakatiya Rudreshwara Ramappa Temple (Warangal) = UNESCO WHS 2021. (9) Charminar + Golconda + Mecca Masjid + Falaknuma Palace at Hyderabad. (10) Hyderabadi biryani + haleem — cuisine icons. POST-2014 state formation — ALL PENDING state demands renewed: (1) GORKHALAND (Darjeeling hill areas, WB); (2) BODOLAND (Assam); (3) VIDARBHA (Maharashtra); (4) HARIT PRADESH / PURVANCHAL / Bundelkhand (UP breakup 4-way per Mayawati 2011); (5) Saurashtra (Gujarat); (6) Mithila (Bihar); (7) Kongu Nadu (TN); (8) Coorg (Karnataka); (9) Greater Tipraland (Tripura); (10) Kosala (Odisha). Politically challenging — each state creation sets precedent. Govt of India wary post-Telangana. NITI AAYOG vs PLANNING COMMISSION (scrapped Jan 2015) — reflects Centre's cooperative-federalism push. EARLIER STATES chronologically: (1) 1953 AP; (2) 1956 big reorganisation; (3) 1960 Maharashtra + Gujarat; (4) 1963 Nagaland; (5) 1966 Haryana; (6) 1971 HP; (7) 1972 Meghalaya/Manipur/Tripura; (8) 1975 Sikkim (22nd); (9) 1987 Mizoram/Arunachal/Goa (25-26-27); (10) 2000 Chhattisgarh (26th)/Uttarakhand/Jharkhand (28th wait — actually 26, 27, 28); (11) 2014 Telangana (29th).

questions.stem: INDIA's LONGEST river that is ENTIRELY WITHIN Indian borders is:

options.option_text: GODAVARI — 1,465 km, 2nd longest in India (after Ganga), entirely within India; 'Dakshina Ganga' (South Ganga); source TRYAMBAKESHWAR Nashik

questions.explanation: GODAVARI — 'DAKSHINA GANGA' (SOUTH GANGA); INDIA's 2ND LONGEST river (after Ganga) + LONGEST entirely within Indian territory. LENGTH: 1,465 km. SOURCE: TRYAMBAKESHWAR (Nashik district, Maharashtra) — one of the 12 JYOTIRLINGAS of Shiva; elevation ~1,067m in Western Ghats. FLOWS: Maharashtra → Telangana → Andhra Pradesh; empties into BAY of BENGAL near ANTARVEDI / RAZOLE (East Godavari / Konaseema district, Andhra) forming large DELTA. MAJOR TRIBUTARIES: Pranhita (largest; joins near Kaleshwaram), Indravati (Chhattisgarh-Odisha-Maharashtra), Sabari (Odisha-AP), Wardha, Wainganga (which join to form Pranhita), Manjra, Penganga. DRAINAGE BASIN: ~3.13 lakh sq km (~10% of India). Largest Peninsular river basin. MAJOR DAMS + PROJECTS: Jayakwadi (Paithan, Maharashtra), Gangapur, Polavaram (Andhra, massive project; under construction decades). Sriram Sagar, Kaleshwaram (world's largest multi-stage lift irrigation, Telangana 2019). FAMOUS CITIES on banks: Nashik, Aurangabad, Bhadrachalam (Ram temple), Rajahmundry (twin bridge), Nanded (Sikh Takht Sachkhand). KUMBH MELA / SIMHASTHA — Nashik (1 of 4 Indian Kumbh cities, along Haridwar + Ujjain + Allahabad). INDIA's RIVERS SYSTEM: (1) HIMALAYAN RIVERS — perennial (fed by glaciers + monsoon; long courses): INDUS SYSTEM — Indus, Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej (5 rivers of Punjab 'pancha-ab' = 5 waters) — most of these flow into Pakistan (Indus Waters Treaty 1960 divides — India gets Eastern 3 Ravi + Beas + Sutlej; Pakistan gets Western 3 Indus + Jhelum + Chenab). GANGA SYSTEM — Ganga (Ganges, 2,525 km, source Gangotri; longest in India INCLUDING Bangladesh), YAMUNA (1,376 km; longest tributary of Ganga; source Yamunotri), Gomati, Ghaghra (Karnali Nepal source), Gandak, Kosi ('sorrow of Bihar' — shifts course; source Tibet), Ramganga, Chambal (Yamuna tributary). BRAHMAPUTRA SYSTEM — Brahmaputra (2,900 km total; 916 km in India as Dihang/Siang/Brahmaputra via Arunachal → Assam → Bangladesh where called Jamuna → joins Ganga as Padma → Bay of Bengal). SOURCE: MANASAROVAR lake Tibet (as YARLUNG TSANGPO). (2) PENINSULAR RIVERS — seasonal, monsoon-fed, shorter, faster. EAST-FLOWING (to Bay of Bengal — form deltas): GODAVARI (1,465 km), KRISHNA (1,400 km, source MAHABALESHWAR MH), KAVERI (800 km, source TALAKAVERI KA), MAHANADI (858 km, Odisha), BRAHMANI, SUBARNAREKHA, PENNA, PENNAR. WEST-FLOWING (to Arabian Sea — form estuaries, no deltas; flow through rifts): NARMADA (1,312 km, source AMARKANTAK MP), TAPI / TAPTI (724 km, source MULTAI MP; Narmada + Tapi flow through RIFT VALLEYS between Vindhya + Satpura). SABARMATI, MAHI, LUNI (only river of Rajasthan; drains into Rann). WEST COAST rivers of Kerala + Karnataka: Periyar, Bharatapuzha, Pamba, Sharavathi (Jog Falls). RIVERS by INDIAN LENGTH: (1) Ganga 2525 km total; ~1300 km in India proper (rest Bangladesh). (2) Godavari 1465 km — longest WHOLLY INDIAN. (3) Yamuna 1376 km. (4) Krishna 1400 km. (5) Narmada 1312 km. (6) Indus 3180 km total, ~710 km in India. (7) Brahmaputra 2900 total, 916 km in India. NATIONAL RIVER: GANGA (declared 2008 by UPA). NAMAMI GANGE (2014, Modi govt) — ₹30,000+ crore cleanup. Ganges is among MOST POLLUTED rivers — sewage, industrial waste, agri runoff, rituals. CLEANING progress mixed. YAMUNA — Delhi stretch dead zone; Yamuna Action Plan. RIVER-LINKING projects proposed (NWDA) — controversial.

options.option_text: MAHARASHTRA (BJP-Shiv Sena, now DEPUTY since Dec 2024 + Devendra Fadnavis CM); UTTAR PRADESH (BJP); WEST BENGAL (TMC); TAMIL NADU (DMK)

questions.explanation: KEY INDIAN STATE CMs (as of April 2025): (1) ANDHRA PRADESH — N. CHANDRABABU NAIDU (TDP, Dec 2024- returning third term after TDP-JSP-BJP alliance won). Previous: Y.S. JAGAN MOHAN REDDY (YSRCP 2019-24). (2) ARUNACHAL PRADESH — PEMA KHANDU (BJP, since 2016). (3) ASSAM — HIMANTA BISWA SARMA (BJP, since May 2021). (4) BIHAR — NITISH KUMAR (JD-U, multiple stints; since Jan 2024 NDA-aligned). (5) CHHATTISGARH — VISHNU DEO SAI (BJP, Dec 2023-, first tribal CM of Chhattisgarh). (6) DELHI — ATISHI (AAP, Sept 2024-; took over after Arvind Kejriwal resigned post-bail; 3rd woman CM of Delhi after Sheila Dikshit + Sushma Swaraj). [Feb 2025: BJP's Rekha Gupta just CM post BJP's election win.] (7) GOA — PRAMOD SAWANT (BJP, since March 2019). (8) GUJARAT — BHUPENDRA PATEL (BJP, since Sep 2021, 2nd term from Dec 2022). (9) HARYANA — NAYAB SINGH SAINI (BJP, since March 2024; Khattar moved to Centre; retained CM post 2024 state election win). (10) HIMACHAL PRADESH — SUKHVINDER SINGH SUKHU (Congress, Dec 2022-). (11) JHARKHAND — HEMANT SOREN (JMM, Dec 2023-; jailed briefly 2024 on ED case; returned post bail + JMM-Cong 2024 state election win). (12) KARNATAKA — SIDDARAMAIAH (Congress, May 2023-). (13) KERALA — PINARAYI VIJAYAN (CPI-M, LDF, since 2016; 2nd term from 2021). (14) MADHYA PRADESH — MOHAN YADAV (BJP, Dec 2023-; first-term OBC CM replacing Shivraj Singh Chouhan). (15) MAHARASHTRA — DEVENDRA FADNAVIS (BJP, Dec 2024-; 3rd term; took over post 2024 Mahayuti win). Previous Eknath Shinde (Shiv Sena, June 2022-Dec 2024) now Deputy CM along with Ajit Pawar NCP. (16) MANIPUR — PRESIDENT's RULE imposed 13 Feb 2025 (after N Biren Singh's BJP regime collapse amid ongoing Meitei-Kuki violence since May 2023). (17) MEGHALAYA — CONRAD SANGMA (NPP, NDA-aligned, March 2018-, 2nd term 2023). (18) MIZORAM — LALDUHOMA (ZPM, Dec 2023-). (19) NAGALAND — NEIPHIU RIO (NDPP, 2018-, multi-term). (20) ODISHA — MOHAN CHARAN MAJHI (BJP, June 2024-; first BJP CM of Odisha; tribal). Previous NAVEEN PATNAIK (BJD, CM 2000-2024, 5 terms — India's 2nd longest-serving CM after Pawan Chamling of Sikkim 1994-2019). (21) PUNJAB — BHAGWANT MANN (AAP, March 2022-). (22) RAJASTHAN — BHAJAN LAL SHARMA (BJP, Dec 2023-, first-term Brahmin). Previous Ashok Gehlot (Cong). (23) SIKKIM — PREM SINGH TAMANG 'PS Golay' (SKM, 2019-, 2nd term 2024). (24) TAMIL NADU — M.K. STALIN (DMK, since 2021; son of M. Karunanidhi). (25) TELANGANA — A. REVANTH REDDY (Congress, Dec 2023-). Previous KCR (BRS). (26) TRIPURA — MANIK SAHA (BJP, 2022-, 2nd term 2023). (27) UTTAR PRADESH — YOGI ADITYANATH (BJP, since March 2017; 2nd term from March 2022). (28) UTTARAKHAND — PUSHKAR SINGH DHAMI (BJP, since July 2021; 2nd term 2022). (29) WEST BENGAL — MAMATA BANERJEE 'Didi' (TMC, since 2011 — 3rd term 2021; longest-serving woman CM in India). 2024 ELECTIONS stability: BJP + allies dominate Centre + 18 states; INDIA bloc (Cong + allies) has Jharkhand, Karnataka, Telangana, HP, J&K, TN. Mixed: Kerala (LDF), Delhi (AAP — just LOST Feb 2025), Odisha (BJP just took), Maha (Mahayuti BJP+SS+NCP). PRESIDENT's RULE in Manipur (from Feb 2025) + usual short stints elsewhere. LIEUTENANT GOVERNORS of UTs with legislatures: Delhi — VINAI K SAXENA; Puducherry — K. KAILASHNATHAN; J&K — MANOJ SINHA. SPEAKERS of LOK SABHA: OM BIRLA (BJP, since 2019). RAJYA SABHA Chair = VP JAGDEEP DHANKHAR (2022-27).
